title: Cech vanishing on a basis with a cofinal set of coverings gives cohomology vanishing (Stacks 01EW, for O_X-modules on a scheme)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ let $\mathcal F|_U$ be the restricted $\mathcal O_U$-module, $(\mathcal F|_U)(W)=\mathcal F(W)$ for $W\subseteq U$ open [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and $H^p(U,-)$ the cohomology of the scheme $U$ (an open subscheme of $X$), the right derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ on $\mathcal O_U$-modules [pqf-def-cohomology]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ and a family $(U_j)_{j\in J}$ of opens with $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ let $\mathcal U=\{U_j\to U\}_{j\in J}$ be the corresponding covering of the Zariski site $X_{\rm Zar}$ (the site of open subschemes of $X$ with inclusions as morphisms and jointly surjective open families as coverings [def-sc-zariski-site]; the fibre product $U_{j_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{j_p}$ is the intersection $U_{j_0\ldots j_p}=U_{j_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{j_p}$), and let $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ be the Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups $W\mapsto\mathcal F(W)$ for $\mathcal U$ (degree $p$ term $\prod_{(j_0,\ldots,j_p)\in J^{p+1}}\mathcal F(U_{j_0\ldots j_p})$, alternating sum of restrictions as differential). Let $\mathcal B$ be a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology, and $\mathrm{Cov}$ a set of such coverings, such that: (1) for every $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$, $U$, every $U_j$ and every $U_{j_0\ldots j_p}$ ($p\ge0$, $j_k\in J$) lie in $\mathcal B$; (2) for every $U\in\mathcal B$ the coverings of $U$ occurring in $\mathrm{Cov}$ are cofinal among all open coverings of $U$: every open covering $U=\bigcup_aV_a$ is refined by some $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$, i.e. every $U_j$ lies in some $V_a$; (3) $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$ and every $p>0$. Then $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)=0$ for every $p>0$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$. (Stacks states this for ringed spaces, with $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ the derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, which equal $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)$ by Lemma 01E1; it is the variant of [lem-weil-pbc-module-cech-vanishing-criterion] (Stacks 01EV) in which only the opens of $\mathcal B$ and the coverings in $\mathrm{Cov}$ occur.)

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EW (label lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696) and its proof (embedding into an injective, Lemma 01EP, Lemma 01EU lemma-ses-cech-h1, dimension shifting); cited in the proof of Lemma 01FF (line 3285). Tag verified in tags/tags: 01EW,cohomology-lemma-cech-vanish-basis.

proof.text: **Step 1 (the induction).** Call an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ *$\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic* if $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$ and every $p>0$, i.e. if $\mathcal G$ satisfies hypothesis (3) of the lemma ($\mathcal B$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ are fixed and satisfy (1) and (2)). For $p\ge1$ let $P(p)$ be the assertion: for every $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$, $H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)=0$. We prove $P(p)$ for all $p\ge1$ by induction on $p$, quantified over all $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic $\mathcal G$ at once (Steps 2-8 for a fixed $\mathcal G$, Step 9 the induction); the lemma is $P(p)$ for $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$, which is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic by (3).

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof ("We will indicate this by saying F has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any U in Cov"; "Since F was an arbitrary O_X-module with vanishing higher Cech cohomology for all U in Cov ... And so on and so forth")

proof.text: **Step 2 (embedding into an injective).** Let $\mathcal G$ be $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic. Since $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], choose a monomorphism $\iota:\mathcal G\to\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I$ an injective object of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $\pi:\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q=\mathcal I/\mathcal G$ be its cokernel in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $0\to\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathcal I\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal Q\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (in an abelian category a monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel, and a cokernel is an epimorphism).

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof, first paragraph ("Choose an embedding F -> I into an injective O_X-module ... Let Q = I/F so that we have a short exact sequence")

proof.text: **Step 3 ($\mathcal I$ is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic).** Every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$, $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$, is a family of opens of $X$ covering the open $U$, i.e. a covering of $X_{\rm Zar}$ of the kind considered in [lem-weil-pbc-module-injective-open-cover-cech-acyclic] (Stacks 01EP). Applied to the injective $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal I$ and to $\mathcal U$, that lemma gives $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$. So $\mathcal I$ is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic.

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof ("By Lemma 01EP I has vanishing higher Cech cohomology for any U in Cov")

proof.text: **Step 4 (the sequence is exact on sections over every member of $\mathcal B$).** Let $W\in\mathcal B$. The sequence $0\to\mathcal G(W)\xrightarrow{\iota_W}\mathcal I(W)\xrightarrow{\pi_W}\mathcal Q(W)\to0$ of abelian groups is exact. Exactness at $\mathcal G(W)$ and $\mathcal I(W)$ (this holds for every open $W$): by Step 2, $\iota$ is a kernel of $\pi$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], and kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $\iota_W$ is injective with image $\ker\pi_W$. Surjectivity of $\pi_W$: let $\Sigma_W$ be the set of the coverings of $W$ that occur in $\mathrm{Cov}$ (the $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_jU_j$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$ with $U=W$). By hypothesis (2), since $W\in\mathcal B$, $\Sigma_W$ is cofinal among the open coverings of $W$: every open covering of $W$ is refined by a member of $\Sigma_W$. Since $\mathcal G$ is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic, $\check H^1(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $\mathcal U\in\Sigma_W$. So [lem-weil-pbc-module-ses-cech-h1-surjective] (Stacks 01EU), applied to $0\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$, the open $W$ and $\Sigma=\Sigma_W$, gives that $\pi_W:\mathcal I(W)\to\mathcal Q(W)$ is surjective.

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof ("By Lemma 01EU and our assumption (2) this sequence gives rise to an exact sequence 0 -> F(U) -> I(U) -> Q(U) -> 0 for every U in B")

proof.text: **Step 5 (short exact sequence of Cech complexes for $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$).** Let $\mathcal U:U=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ be in $\mathrm{Cov}$, a covering of $X_{\rm Zar}$ [def-sc-zariski-site] whose fibre products are the intersections $U_{j_0\ldots j_p}$. The morphisms $\iota,\pi$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules are in particular morphisms of the underlying presheaves of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$, so they induce morphisms of Cech complexes $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)$ (functoriality, part (e) of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]), with composite $0$. In degree $p\ge0$ this sequence is the product over $(j_0,\ldots,j_p)\in J^{p+1}$ of the sequences $0\to\mathcal G(U_{j_0\ldots j_p})\to\mathcal I(U_{j_0\ldots j_p})\to\mathcal Q(U_{j_0\ldots j_p})\to0$. By hypothesis (1) every $U_{j_0\ldots j_p}$ lies in $\mathcal B$, so each of these sequences is short exact by Step 4 (with $W=U_{j_0\ldots j_p}$); a product of short exact sequences of abelian groups is short exact (kernel and image of a product of homomorphisms are the products of the kernels and images); in degrees $p<0$ all terms are $0$. Hence $0\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of abelian groups, short exactness of complexes being degreewise [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact].

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof ("Hence for any U in Cov we get a short exact sequence of Cech complexes ... since each term in the Cech complex is made up out of a product of values over elements of B by assumption (1)")

proof.text: **Step 6 ($\mathcal Q$ is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic).** For every $\mathcal U\in\mathrm{Cov}$, the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] of the short exact sequence of complexes of Step 5 contains, for each $p\ge1$, the exact piece $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\to\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)\xrightarrow{\delta^p}\check H^{p+1}(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. The left term is $0$ by Step 3 and the right term is $0$ because $\mathcal G$ is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic and $p+1>0$; so $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal Q)=0$. Thus $\mathcal Q$ is again a $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof ("In particular we have a long exact sequence of Cech cohomology groups for any open covering U in Cov. This implies that Q is also an O_X-module with vanishing higher Cech cohomology for all U in Cov")

proof.text: **Step 7 (restriction to $U\in\mathcal B$).** Let $U\in\mathcal B$ (an open subset of $X$). By [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives] (1), restriction $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A|_U$, $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, is additive and exact; applied to the short exact sequence of Step 2 it gives a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G|_U\xrightarrow{\iota|_U}\mathcal I|_U\xrightarrow{\pi|_U}\mathcal Q|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. By part (2) of the same lemma, $\mathcal I|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module. Moreover $\Gamma(U,\mathcal A|_U)=(\mathcal A|_U)(U)=\mathcal A(U)$ and $(\pi|_U)_U=\pi_U$ by the definition of the restricted module [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits].

source.place: Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 496) (2), H^p(U,F) = H^p(U,F|_U), used to pass from the derived functors of Gamma(U,-) on Mod(O_X) in 01EW to cohomology of the scheme U

proof.text: **Step 8 (cohomology of $U$ as derived functors).** For $U\in\mathcal B$ the open subscheme $U$ is a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $H^n(U,-)=R^nv$ ($n\ge0$) are the right derived functors of the global sections functor $v=\Gamma(U,-):\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\textit{Ab}$, $\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A(U)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]; this makes sense because $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is an abelian category with enough injectives [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives] (applied to the scheme $U$), and $v$ is additive and left exact, since kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. (Whether $v$ takes values in abelian groups or in $\mathcal O_U(U)$-modules does not change the underlying groups $R^nv(\mathcal A)$, hence not their vanishing.)

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof, second paragraph ("Next, we look at the long exact cohomology sequence ... for any U in B")

proof.text: **Step 9 (dimension shifting).** Let $U\in\mathcal B$ and apply the long exact sequence of the right derived functors $H^n(U,-)=R^nv$ of Step 8 [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal I|_U\to\mathcal Q|_U\to0$ of Step 7; since $\mathcal I|_U$ is injective in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ (Step 7), $H^n(U,\mathcal I|_U)=0$ for $n>0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] (Stacks 015B). Case $p=1$: the piece $H^0(U,\mathcal I|_U)\to H^0(U,\mathcal Q|_U)\to H^1(U,\mathcal G|_U)\to H^1(U,\mathcal I|_U)=0$ is exact, and under the natural isomorphism $R^0v\cong v$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] its first map is $v(\pi|_U)=\pi_U:\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal Q(U)$ (Step 7), which is surjective by Step 4 with $W=U\in\mathcal B$; hence $H^1(U,\mathcal G|_U)=0$. This holds for every $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic $\mathcal G$ and every $U\in\mathcal B$, which is $P(1)$. Case $p\ge2$, assuming $P(p-1)$: the piece $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q|_U)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)\to H^p(U,\mathcal I|_U)=0$ is exact, and $H^{p-1}(U,\mathcal Q|_U)=0$ by $P(p-1)$ applied to $\mathcal Q$, which is $\mathrm{Cov}$-acyclic by Step 6, and to $U\in\mathcal B$; hence $H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)=0$, which is $P(p)$. By induction $P(p)$ holds for all $p\ge1$; with $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ (Step 1) this is the lemma.

source.place: Lemma 01EW (lemma-cech-vanish-basis, line 1696), proof, second paragraph ("Since I is injective we have H^n(U,I) = 0 for n > 0 (Derived Categories Lemma 015B). By the above we see that H^0(U,I) -> H^0(U,Q) is surjective and hence H^1(U,F) = 0 ... also H^1(U,Q) = 0 since Q is another of these sheaves ... H^2(U,F) = 0. And so on and so forth.")
